gallery.filename: Aerial view of USS Mindanao (ARG-3) after the explosion of USS Mount Hood (AE-11) at Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944.jpg
gallery.title: File:Aerial view of USS Mindanao (ARG-3) after the explosion of USS Mount Hood (AE-11) at Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944.jpg
gallery.credit: U.S. Navy photo NH 95405, copied from the War Diary, Manus Naval Base, for November 1944.
gallery.source: Aerial view of USS Mindanao (ARG-3) after the explosion of USS Mount Hood (AE-11) at Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944
gallery.description: Explosion of the U.S. Navy ammunition ship USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands, 10 November 1944: Small craft gathered around the internal combustion engine repair ship USS Mindanao (ARG-3) during salvage and rescue efforts shortly after Mount Hood blew up about 350 yards away from Mindanao's port side. Mindanao, and seven motor minesweepers (YMS) moored to her starboard side, were damaged by the blast, as were the attack transport USS Alhena (AKA-9), in the photo's top left center, and the destroyer escort USS Oberrender (DE-344), in top right. Note the extensive oil slick, with tracks through it made by small craft.

gallery.filename: USS Mindanao (ARG-3) damaged by explosion of USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944.jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Mindanao (ARG-3) damaged by explosion of USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944.jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Navy, copied from the War Diary, Manus Naval Base, for November 1944.
gallery.credit: Official U.S. Navy photo NH 96174 from the U.S. Navy Naval History and Heritage Command
gallery.source: USS Mindanao (ARG-3) damaged by explosion of USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944
gallery.description:
Explosion of the U.S. Navy ammunition ship USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands, 10 November 1944: Salvage and rescue work underway on the repair ship USS Mindanao (ARG-3) shortly after Mount Hood blew up about 350 yards away. Note heavy damage to Mindanao's hull and superstructure, including large holes from fragment impacts. View looks forward from alongside her port quarter. Small craft alongside or nearby include (from left) YPB-6 (probable identification), two LCVPs and YPB-7.
Mindanao had 180 crewmen killed and injured by this explosion. She was under repair until 21 December 1944.
categories: Seeadler Harbor in World War II
